newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ sees 1.3 percent growth in March 1997 year.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ sees 1.3 percent growth in March 1997 year.

text.p: The Reserve Bank in its six- monthly monetary policy statement on Tuesday forecast New Zealand point-to-point economic growth at 1.3 percent in the year to March 1997.
It forecast growth of 2.6 percent in the year to March 1998, and 2.1 percent in the year to March 1999.
In its previous forecasts in September, the bank projected production based GDP growth rates of 2.0 percent on a March quarter on March quarter 1997 basis, and 2.6 percent in 1998.
In its December economic forecasts, Treasury forecast 3.1 percent growth on the same basis for 1996/97 and 3.4 percent the following year.
The RBNZ's latest projections were finalised before the formation of the National-New Zealand First Party coalition government last week.

The RBNZ said the assumed fiscal policy stance and the assumed level of monetary conditions were judged to be broadly unchanged compared with the assumptions made in September, and thus had a neutral impact on the projections.
The RBNZ projected annual average growth rates of 1.6 percent in the March 1997 year, 2.3 percent in 1998, and 2.3 percent in 1999.
The bank forecast point-to-point employment growth of 1.9 percent in the March 1997 year, 0.2 percent in 1998 and 1.1 percent in 1999.
It saw a seasonally adjusted unemployment rate of 6.7 percent in the March quarter 1997 year, 7.0 percent in 1998 and 6.7 percent in 1999.
The bank forecast the current account as a percentage of GDP at -4.7 percent in the year to March 1997, -4.8 percent in 1998 and -5.3 percent in 1999.
The government's operating surplus as a percentage of GDP was projected at 2.1 percent in the year to June 1997, 1.6 percent in 1998 and 1.9 percent in 1999.
